reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Orphan Annie nuclei plus psammoma bodies mean papillary thyroid cancer
Follicular cancer diagnosis requires capsular or vascular invasion histologically
Raised calcium with suppressed PTH means malignancy PTHrP, not parathyroid disease
Medullary cancer calcitonin links to MEN2 syndromes
reference.pathophysiology: Autoimmune destruction or stimulation remodels thyroid function while mutational drivers (BRAF, RET, RAS families) transform follicular or C cells along distinct pathways. Parathyroid chief cell adenomas escape calcium sensing, and chronic renal stimulation hyperplasias all glands, explaining primary versus secondary biochemical patterns.
additionalInvestigations: TSH with free T4 and anti TPO or TSH receptor antibodies
Ultrasound risk stratification with fine needle aspiration
Calcium, phosphate, PTH, vitamin D and urinary calcium panel
